question: Estimate Punctual Pros revenue from public filings
html:
Punctual Pros revenue estimate

FY2025 pro forma revenue is est. ~$22M (range $16-28M), medium confidence. That is about $18M from Pennsylvania and $3-5M from the New Jersey add-on, Horvath Home Services (Punctual Pros public filings).

Three methods, one range

MethodBasisRevenue est.
PPP loan (2019 base)$745,985 loan implies ~$3.58M payroll; payroll at 30-40% of revenue~$9-12M (2019, Rohrer only)
Headcount and wages~113 staff x ~$76K Lancaster wage; 40-45% labor ratio~$18-22M PA run-rate at the April 3, 2024 entry
FDD territory mapping25 territories mapped to Item 19 quartiles~$12-19M PA; ~$3-5M NJ (FY2025)
  • The blended PA figure is ~$18M (range $12-24M), medium confidence (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • Horvath's 2019 base was est. ~$3-4M, from a $251,894 PPP loan (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • Revenue roughly doubled from the 2019 PPP base by the deal, est.

Territory economics

  • The 2026 FDD lists show 25 operated territories: 19 PA and 6 NJ. Confidence is high (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • Revenue per territory is est. ~$0.9M, against system averages of $0.61M (One Hour) and $0.66M (Ben Franklin). Confidence is low.
  • This suggests above-system productivity. Verify it before relying on it.

Margin and leverage context

  • Royalty (6%) plus brand fund (~1.2-1.5%) takes ~7.2-7.5% of revenue. That is ~$1.6M a year, est.
  • The fees cap adjusted EBITDA margins near 8-14%. Adjusted EBITDA is est. ~$1.8-3.1M (central ~$2.6M), low confidence.
  • PGIM Private Credit Fund's June 30, 2026 10-Q shows a first-lien loan to Punctual Pros Midco at SOFR+5.00% (8.73%), maturing March 26, 2029.
  • Funded amount: $4.83M, marked at ~98.6% of par.
  • Unfunded commitment: $1.4M (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • The disclosed loan is modest against est. EBITDA. Full debt quantum is not confirmed from public data.

Caveats

  • The ~113 headcount comes from the task brief and was not re-verified (BSP firm profile).
  • The labor-ratio assumptions are industry rules of thumb, not company data.
  • Filings were verified on September 24, 2026: 29 of 30 sampled items were confirmed and 1 was removed.
  • Management accounts would replace all three estimates. These are monthly P&L by territory and brand for FY2025, plus the year-to-date 2026 figures.

Next actions

  • Pull FY2025 audited or management financials and reconcile them to the ~$22M estimate, by state and brand.
  • Confirm current headcount and loaded labor cost to test the 40-45% labor ratio.
  • Compare revenue per territory to Authority Brands Item 19 quartiles. Identify which territories drive the gap above system averages.
  • Confirm total debt and the delayed-draw status with the lender group.

# Punctual Pros revenue estimate

FY2025 pro forma revenue is est. **~$22M (range $16-28M)**, medium confidence. That is about $18M from Pennsylvania and $3-5M from the New Jersey add-on, Horvath Home Services (Punctual Pros public filings).

## Three methods, one range

| Method | Basis | Revenue est. |
|---|---|---|
| PPP loan (2019 base) | $745,985 loan implies ~$3.58M payroll; payroll at 30-40% of revenue | ~$9-12M (2019, Rohrer only) |
| Headcount and wages | ~113 staff x ~$76K Lancaster wage; 40-45% labor ratio | ~$18-22M PA run-rate at the April 3, 2024 entry |
| FDD territory mapping | 25 territories mapped to Item 19 quartiles | ~$12-19M PA; ~$3-5M NJ (FY2025) |

- The blended PA figure is ~$18M (range $12-24M), medium confidence (Punctual Pros public filings).
- Horvath's 2019 base was est. ~$3-4M, from a $251,894 PPP loan (Punctual Pros public filings).
- Revenue roughly doubled from the 2019 PPP base by the deal, est.

## Territory economics

- The 2026 FDD lists show 25 operated territories: 19 PA and 6 NJ. Confidence is high (Punctual Pros public filings).
- Revenue per territory is est. ~$0.9M, against system averages of $0.61M (One Hour) and $0.66M (Ben Franklin). Confidence is low.
- This suggests above-system productivity. Verify it before relying on it.

## Margin and leverage context

- Royalty (6%) plus brand fund (~1.2-1.5%) takes ~7.2-7.5% of revenue. That is ~$1.6M a year, est.
- The fees cap adjusted EBITDA margins near 8-14%. Adjusted EBITDA is est. ~$1.8-3.1M (central ~$2.6M), low confidence.
- PGIM Private Credit Fund's June 30, 2026 10-Q shows a first-lien loan to Punctual Pros Midco at SOFR+5.00% (8.73%), maturing March 26, 2029.
  - Funded amount: $4.83M, marked at ~98.6% of par.
  - Unfunded commitment: $1.4M (Punctual Pros public filings).
- The disclosed loan is modest against est. EBITDA. Full debt quantum is not confirmed from public data.

## Caveats

- The ~113 headcount comes from the task brief and was not re-verified (BSP firm profile).
- The labor-ratio assumptions are industry rules of thumb, not company data.
- Filings were verified on September 24, 2026: 29 of 30 sampled items were confirmed and 1 was removed.
- Management accounts would replace all three estimates. These are monthly P&L by territory and brand for FY2025, plus the year-to-date 2026 figures.

## Next actions

- Pull FY2025 audited or management financials and reconcile them to the ~$22M estimate, by state and brand.
- Confirm current headcount and loaded labor cost to test the 40-45% labor ratio.
- Compare revenue per territory to Authority Brands Item 19 quartiles. Identify which territories drive the gap above system averages.
- Confirm total debt and the delayed-draw status with the lender group.
